text_blocks.snippet: Federal prosecutors and local authorities recently issued warnings about a U.S. Attorney's Office Phone Spoofing Scam where callers spoof official numbers, use real staff names, and demand immediate payments.

snippet_links.text: U.S. Attorney's Office Phone Spoofing Scam

text_blocks.snippet: 📊 Common Active Scams in Central Illinois

list.snippet: 📱 Government & Law Enforcement Impersonation: Scammers spoof the U.S. Attorney's Office, local sheriff's departments, or the DMV/IDOT, claiming you have missed jury duty, arrest warrants, or unpaid tolls/traffic tickets. They demand panic-driven digital payments (like Bitcoin or gift cards).
⚡ Utility "Slamming": Fraudsters call local businesses and residents claiming to be with Energy Choice or Amarin Choice, trying to trick you into switching or revealing rate details.
🏡 Door-to-Door & Repair Scams: Following seasonal severe weather, transient con artists canvas neighborhoods offering fast home or business repairs, demanding large cash deposits upfront.
🎁 Sweepstakes & Prize Traps: Fake winning notifications that require an upfront "fee" or tax payment to release the funds.
Practice the pause: Take a breath when someone demands urgent action or secrecy; real agencies give you time to verify.
Never pay over the phone: Government agencies, courts, and utilities will never call, text, or email demanding immediate payment, Bitcoin, or gift card numbers.
Hang up and verify: Look up the official public number of the agency or utility yourself and call them directly rather than trusting caller ID (which is easily spoofed).
Don't click links: Ignore unsolicited text messages about toll violations, package deliveries, or DMV fees.
Illinois Attorney General's Scam Hotline: Call 1-800-243-0618.
State Text Scams: Forward fraudulent state texts to scamalert@illinois.gov (or check guidance via the Illinois IDOT Text Scam Alert).
Better Business Bureau: Reach out to the BBB of Central Illinois to check on suspicious trends or report local incidents.
